- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model may lag; adjust forecast to align with 3-day moving average of true values.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overestimates mean; use 15-day EWMA or 20-day SMA as anchor.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction proportional to sentiment magnitude (e.g., -0.15×sentiment for each day).
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, use 10-day rolling average of true values as baseline; don’t rely on 30d model unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
